'''Matt Visser''' ({{post-nominals|country=NZL|FRSNZ}}) is a mathematics professor at [[Victoria University of Wellington]], in New Zealand.

==Career==
Visser completed a PhD at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], supervised by [[Mary K. Gaillard]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Matt Visser - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=195970 |access-date=2023-04-09 |website=mathgenealogy.org}}</ref>

Visser's research interests include [[general relativity]], [[quantum field theory]] and [[cosmology]].

Visser has produced a large number of research papers on the subject of [[wormhole]]s, gravitational horizons and notably the emerging subject of [[acoustic metric]]s.

He is the author of the reference book on the current state of wormhole theory, ''Lorentzian Wormholes — from Einstein to Hawking'' (1996) and co-editor of ''Artificial Black Holes'' (2002).

== Awards ==
In 2013 Visser was awarded the [[Dan Walls]] Medal by the New Zealand Institute of Physics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NZIP Award Recipients – New Zealand Institute of Physics |url=https://nzip.org.nz/about-nzip/nzip-award-recipients/ |access-date=2023-03-16 |language=en-US}}</ref>

*M Novello, Matt Visser & G E Volovik, [https://www.worldcat.org/oclc/51548418 ''Artificial Black Holes'' (2002)] {{ISBN|978-981-02-4807-9}}
